newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call rates retreat after touching 10.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Indian call rates retreat after touching 10.5 pct.

text.p: Indian call money rates closed higher at 9.00-9.50 percent on Thursday compared to the day's opening levels of 8.50-9.25 percent, dealers said.
Call rates touched a peak of 10.5 percent during the day but most of the day's deals were in the region of 9.0-10.0 percent. The lowest level was 8.50 percent, dealers said.
The call rates are expected to ease on on Friday as the repurchase of previous repo auction is expected to inject 30 billion rupees into the system, a dealer said.

Thursday's repo auction attracted only bids for 9.0 billion rupees. Call rates should open softer - at 6.0 to 7.0 percent - on Friday and the absence of the State Bank of India (SBI) would not be felt on Friday, some dealers said.
SBI kept away from the market on Thursday.
SBI gives a lending support to the market, while its dollar purchases adds liquidity to the system, dealers said.
The securities market witnessed dull trading. The sellers were sticking to the earlier prices, a dealer said.
The volume on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) fell to 1.5 billion rupees from the previous 3.58 rupees, a NSE delaer said.
